question: Why is observation often more reliable than interviews in research?

options.A: It allows researchers to control what the participants say
options.B: It takes much less time and fewer resources to complete
options.C: It captures actual behavior rather than just reported behavior
options.D: It is completely free of any human bias or error

explanation: People sometimes misremember or forget details in interviews, but direct observation lets you see what is truly happening in real time.

question: Which of these is a very common nursing diagnosis for a patient struggling with a severe phobia?

options.A: Impaired Gas Exchange
options.B: Deficient Fluid Volume
options.C: Risk for Infection
options.D: Ineffective Coping

explanation: Because phobias rely heavily on avoidance rather than healthy problem-solving, 'Ineffective Coping' fits right in your care plan.

question: Why are prophylactic antibiotics usually given within one hour before the surgical incision is made?

options.A: To allow the surgical team time to perform hand scrubbing rituals
options.B: To neutralize any bacteria already present in the circulating air
options.C: To prevent the patient from experiencing nausea while on the operating table
options.D: To ensure peak tissue concentration of the drug when the skin is opened

explanation: Timing is everything! Giving the drug right before surgery means the antibiotic is fully active in the tissues the exact second the skin opens.

question: Why is early identification of genetic risks important for nurses in primary healthcare?

options.A: It prevents patients from developing infectious diseases
options.B: It allows for proactive education and early risk reduction
options.C: It completely cures the genetic condition before birth
options.D: It eliminates the need for any further medical testing

explanation: Spotting risks early gives healthcare providers the chance to guide families and prevent severe complications before symptoms appear. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h1)

question: For about how long can an unfertilized egg survive after being released during ovulation?

options.A: 12 to 24 hours
options.B: 5 to 7 days
options.C: 48 to 72 hours
options.D: 1 month

explanation: An egg has a very short shelf life—just 12 to 24 hours after ovulation—which is why timing is everything for fertilization!

question: What is the standard measurement of the biparietal diameter (BPD) in a full-term baby?

options.A: 9.5 cm
options.B: 8.0 cm

explanation: The biparietal diameter—the distance from one side of the head to the other—is roughly 9.5 centimeters at full term. You'll see this number all the time on ultrasound scans!

question: A patient comes in after a clandestine abortion with a high fever, smelly vaginal discharge, and lower tummy pain. What is the most likely problem?

options.A: Normal postpartum involution
options.B: Pelvic inflammatory sepsis
options.C: Uncomplicated uterine atony
options.D: Primary ovarian hyperstimulation

explanation: Fever plus foul-smelling discharge is a red flag for infection. Unsterile instruments easily introduce bacteria right into the uterus, leading quickly to pelvic sepsis. Great clinical spotting!

question: Imagine a nurse is testing a new handwashing technique and makes sure every ward uses the exact same water temperature and soap brand. Why do this?

options.A: To punish wards that do not follow hospital rules
options.B: To prove that water temperature is the only cause of illness
options.C: To control outside variables that could affect infection rates
options.D: To save money on purchasing hospital cleaning supplies

explanation: Exactly right! By keeping things like water and soap the same, you make sure any change in infection rates is truly because of the new technique, not random outside factors.

question: What technology does an autoclave use to make infectious medical waste safe?

options.A: Dry microwave pulses
options.B: Deep freezing cold
options.C: High-pressure steam
options.D: Ultraviolet radiation

explanation: Autoclaves use high-pressure steam and intense heat to wipe out harmful microorganisms effectively. You'll see these in action often!

question: Which hormone unlocks cells so glucose can move in from the blood?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Glucagon
options.C: Thyroxine
options.D: Cortisol

explanation: Think of insulin as the golden key that unlocks cell doors, letting glucose step inside from the bloodstream to provide energy.

question: What usually happens if food travels through the small intestine much faster than normal?

options.A: Increased vitamin storage in the liver
options.B: Reduced nutrient absorption and diarrhea
options.C: Higher than normal blood sugar spikes
options.D: Enhanced breakdown of complex proteins

explanation: When food rushes through too fast, digestive enzymes and cells don't get enough time to do their job, leaving unabsorbed nutrients to pull extra water into the stool.

question: How does the nasal cavity manage to warm up cold inspired air so effectively?

options.A: Friction from the turbinates generates constant physical heat
options.B: A rich network of blood vessels in the submucosa transfers body heat
options.C: Inhaled oxygen undergoes rapid chemical combustion inside the meatus
options.D: Specialized sweat glands inside the nostrils pump thermal energy

explanation: The lamina propria contains a massive supply of blood vessels that radiate heat, warming the air as it swirls past. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why do pure scare tactics usually fail in teenage drug education programs?

options.A: Adolescents lack the physical ability to listen to spoken English instructions
options.B: Teens may find the exaggerated warnings do not match their real-world observations
options.C: Young people prefer reading detailed legal textbooks over listening to talks
options.D: Scare tactics automatically cure physical tolerance within twenty-four hours

explanation: When young people see friends using substances without immediate disaster, over-the-top scare stories lose all credibility. Honest, factual education works best!

question: Which of the following describes colony morphology?

options.A: Measuring the exact temperature inside a laboratory incubator
options.B: Weighing a glass beaker before adding liquid nutrient broth
options.C: Observing the color and shape of a microbial colony on an agar plate
options.D: Counting the number of student desks in a microbiology classroom

explanation: Spot on! Colony morphology is simply looking at the physical traits of a bacterial colony, like its color, texture, and shape.

question: Why is it so important to figure out the exact type of prostatitis a patient has?

options.A: It indicates that immediate surgical removal of the prostate is needed
options.B: It prevents the future development of benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.C: It proves whether the patient has concurrent testicular cancer
options.D: It dictates whether antibiotics or non-infectious management is required

explanation: Brilliant! Bacterial infections need antibiotics, while other types of pelvic pain need a totally different, non-infectious treatment plan.

question: Why are low-molecular-weight heparins so convenient for patients compared to standard heparin?

options.A: They last for an entire month with just one injection
options.B: They never cause any bleeding or immune reactions
options.C: They can be mixed directly into drinking water for easy mornings
options.D: They use standard weight-based doses without needing routine aPTT blood tests

explanation: That's the beauty of LMWH! Because the dose is predictable based on the patient's weight, patients can take them easily without constant pinpricks for aPTT tests.

question: What is the main purpose of regulatory bodies like the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria?

options.A: To manage the commercial business accounts of private hospitals
options.B: To protect the public by ensuring safe and competent nursing practice
options.C: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for local distribution
options.D: To decide which political party wins national health elections

explanation: Spot on! Professional councils exist primarily to keep the public safe by setting high educational and ethical standards for all practicing nurses. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h7)

question: A patient asks why their new antibiotic must be taken strictly with meals. What is the best way to explain this?

options.A: Taking it with food optimizes effectiveness and minimizes stomach upset
options.B: Food prevents the capsule from dissolving too early in the esophagus
options.C: Food chemically inactivates the bacteria before the drug reaches them
options.D: Meals are required to speed up the clearance of the drug through the kidneys

explanation: Some drugs are tough on the tummy or need food to absorb right. Explaining this helps patients stick to their routine without bellyaches.

question: What is the main goal of Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) compared to basic health education?

options.A: Promoting and sustaining healthy community practices
options.B: Reducing the cost of pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Writing medical records for hospital filing
options.D: Increasing the number of operating theatres

explanation: You got this! BCC goes beyond just sharing facts—it actively helps communities adopt and stick to healthy habits for the long run.

question: Which of the following is an example of non-verbal communication?

options.A: Giving spoken instructions over the phone
options.B: Reading a printed pamphlet out loud
options.C: Using medical jargon during a lecture
options.D: Body posture and facial expressions

explanation: Non-verbal communication involves physical cues like body language, posture, and facial expressions rather than spoken words. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h3)

question: How should a washed diaphragm be stored after it dries?

options.A: In its designated storage case away from heat and sunlight
options.B: Wrapped tightly in a plastic bag inside the kitchen freezer
options.C: At the bottom of a handbag without any protective covering
options.D: Hanging openly on a bathroom wall hook exposed to light

explanation: Keeping it in its cool, dark storage case protects the material from heat and sunlight, helping it last a long time.

question: By about what percentage does total blood volume increase in a normal pregnancy?
explanation: Spot on! Blood volume almost doubles to nourish the baby and protect the mother from normal blood loss during childbirth.

question: What is the most important assessment for a nurse to make right after giving a rescue bronchodilator?

options.A: Capillary refill time in the fingers
options.B: Lung sounds and breathing effort
options.C: Deep tendon reflexes in the knees
options.D: Bowel sounds in all four quadrants

explanation: Since bronchodilators open up tight airways, listening to the patient's chest and watching their breathing effort is the quickest way to see if the treatment worked.

question: What makes contraceptive implants a type of LARC (Long-Acting Reversible Contraception) method?

options.A: They must be replaced every month by a skilled surgeon
options.B: They provide multi-year protection without requiring daily user action
options.C: They permanently destroy ovarian function after a single injection
options.D: They require daily oral doses to maintain steady hormone levels

explanation: You've got this! LARC simply means the device works continuously for years on its own, but can also be easily removed whenever the client wants to get pregnant.

question: In immunology, what exactly is an antigen?

options.A: A medication used to lower systemic inflammation
options.B: A foreign substance that triggers an immune response
options.C: A physical barrier found in human skin layers
options.D: A white blood cell that produces Y-shaped proteins

explanation: Great job! An antigen is any foreign molecule that sounds the alarm and gets your immune cells ready for battle.

question: When checking lab results, which finding usually tells you the patient's body is actively fighting off an infection?

options.A: Low platelet concentration levels
options.B: Reduced blood urea nitrogen
options.C: Elevated white blood cell count
options.D: Decreased red blood cell count

explanation: You got it! A high white blood cell count (leukocytosis) means the bone marrow is pumping out extra soldiers to tackle invading germs.

question: Why is a CT scan usually the go-to emergency test for sudden head injuries?

options.A: It has no radiation at all
options.B: It shows the finest details of nerve fibers
options.C: It is fast and great at showing fresh bleeding
options.D: It uses strong magnets instead of radiation

explanation: CT scans are quick and very sensitive to fresh blood, which is a lifesaver in emergency rooms.

question: Which induration measurement is considered positive for a patient with no known risk factors for tuberculosis?

options.A: 15 millimeters or more
options.B: 5 millimeters or more
options.C: 10 millimeters or more
options.D: 20 millimeters or more

explanation: For healthy individuals with no known exposure risks, the cut-off threshold for a positive test is 15 millimeters or greater. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h6)

question: What is the first thing a community health nurse should do when an unusual cluster of sick people appears?

options.A: Wait several months to see if the symptoms disappear on their own
options.B: Organize an international press conference in the capital city
options.C: Verify the diagnosis and confirm that an outbreak is actually occurring
options.D: Close all schools and markets in the entire country permanently

explanation: Before sounding any alarms, always confirm your facts and verify the diagnosis first. Good nursing practice!

question: Why do first-generation antihistamines make patients so sleepy, while newer ones usually do not?

options.A: Second-generation drugs are broken down entirely in the stomach.
options.B: First-generation drugs cross the blood-brain barrier easily.
options.C: First-generation drugs reduce blood pressure too quickly.
options.D: Second-generation drugs contain natural caffeine additives.

explanation: Exactly! Because they easily slip into the central nervous system, first-gen drugs cause that heavy drowsiness we all know. Newer drugs are designed to stay out of the brain.

question: What must a nurse always do before starting any care in a patient's home?

options.A: Publishing the care plan in a national newspaper
options.B: Receiving written approval from local community leaders
options.C: Consulting the hospital board of directors
options.D: Obtaining proper informed consent from the patient

explanation: Always! Respecting our patients means getting their clear okay before doing any checks or procedures.

question: Why might a patient with a cyst test negative on a routine antibody blood test?

options.A: A thick, intact cyst wall can prevent antigens from triggering a strong immune response
options.B: Human antibodies cannot bind to parasite proteins
options.C: Antibodies only appear after the cyst has completely dissolved
options.D: Blood tests only detect adult tapeworms living in the intestines

explanation: If the outer wall seals the cyst tightly, very little leaks out into the blood to trigger antibodies, leading to false negatives.

question: When a drainage tube gets blocked, which of these actions is completely WRONG and dangerous?

options.A: Pushing a partially dislodged tube back into the body cavity
options.B: Checking the entire length of the tubing for accidental kinks
options.C: Inspecting the tube for visible blood clots or mucus plugs
options.D: Notifying the medical team if output remains absent

explanation: You got it! Pushing a slipped tube back inside drags surface bacteria straight into sterile tissues. Always check with your senior or doctor first.

question: What is another name for the Pouch of Douglas in female anatomy?

options.A: Rectouterine pouch
options.B: Broad ligament recess
options.C: Vesicouterine pouch
options.D: Parametrial space

explanation: You've got this! We call it the rectouterine pouch because it sits right between the rectum and the uterus. Simple and straightforward!

question: What is a major drawback of relying only on traditional lectures in nursing training?

options.A: It takes too much time to cover basic medical definitions
options.B: It prevents the instructor from using any visual aids like slides
options.C: It can leave students passive and rarely tests their practical clinical skills
options.D: It requires every student to have a private computer in the hall

explanation: Lectures are great for blasting through a lot of theory quickly, but they don't give you much hands-on practice or test your real-time clinical judgment.

question: What practical challenge does a crowded family compound present to a woman wanting family planning?

options.A: Too much free time to read medical journals
options.B: An inability to visit the local market for food
options.C: Frequent visits from government health inspectors
options.D: A lack of privacy to safely store birth control items

explanation: That's right! Living with many relatives, including in-laws, makes finding a private hiding spot for pills or injectables quite tough.

question: A patient who received a light sedative for a joint scan is awake and asking to go home. What must you confirm before discharge?

options.A: That all physical pain in the joint has completely disappeared
options.B: That the patient has successfully voided a large amount of radioactive urine
options.C: That the radiologist has already completed the final written diagnostic report
options.D: That the patient has stable vital signs, a clear airway, and a responsible escort home

explanation: Sedatives can mess with a person's reflexes and clear thinking for hours. Always make sure they have stable vitals and a trusted adult to take them home safely.

question: What is a major long-term risk of persistent, chronic inflammation in the body?

options.A: Rapid and permanent healing of all damaged joints
options.B: Progressive tissue destruction and organ dysfunction
options.C: Complete prevention of future bacterial infections
options.D: Immediate disappearance of all white blood cells

explanation: Chronic inflammation causes ongoing immune activity that slowly breaks down healthy tissue and impairs organ function. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h8)

question: A nurse discovers that a struggling patient in the ward cannot buy their prescribed antibiotics. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advocate for the patient by contacting the social welfare unit for an exemption
options.B: Reprimand the patient for coming to the hospital without money
options.C: Ignore the situation because financial matters are outside nursing duties
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately from the hospital ward

explanation: You nailed it! As patient advocates, nurses bridge the gap by connecting vulnerable patients with social welfare so they can get their meds without delay.

question: Why do nurses teach patients to use dental floss along with brushing?

options.A: To scrub the tongue and get rid of white coatings
options.B: To push fluoride paste straight down into the tooth roots
options.C: To polish the flat chewing surfaces of the back molars
options.D: To clean out food and plaque from tight spaces between teeth

explanation: Toothbrush bristles are great, but they can't squeeze into the tight spots between teeth. Flossing finishes the job for a truly clean mouth!

question: Why is starting ORT right at home so important for community health?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any professional medical checkups
options.B: It prevents family members from catching the same stomach bug
options.C: It guarantees that the underlying viral infection will disappear overnight
options.D: It stops dehydration from progressing to a dangerous stage before reaching a clinic

explanation: Every minute counts! Giving fluids immediately at home stops mild fluid loss from turning into a life-threatening emergency before the family even reaches the hospital.

question: What are the three components of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Vector, vaccine, and immunity
options.B: Agent, host, and environment
options.C: Bacteria, virus, and fungus
options.D: Primary, secondary, and tertiary

explanation: The classic epidemiological model uses the agent, host, and environment to explain how diseases are transmitted. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h5)

question: In maternal health, what does 'morbidity' mean?

options.A: The death of a woman while pregnant or within forty-two days of delivery
options.B: The total number of pregnant women admitted to a tertiary hospital
options.C: Any infection contracted by a newborn baby during the first week of life
options.D: Any health condition caused or worsened by pregnancy and childbirth

explanation: Think of morbidity simply as the illnesses, injuries, or health struggles that happen because of pregnancy—distinct from maternal mortality, which means death. You've got this!

question: Which measure is most effective for controlling vector-borne diseases like malaria in a community?

options.A: Washing hospital floors with scented detergent twice a day
options.B: Eliminating stagnant water breeding sites and using bed nets
options.C: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics to every healthy adult
options.D: Replacing all plastic medical equipment with stainless steel

explanation: Vector control targets the insects that transmit parasites by destroying their breeding grounds and preventing bites. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h7)

question: Which of these conditions makes taking a bladder anticholinergic unsafe?

options.A: Type 2 diabetes
options.B: Lower back pain
options.C: Mild hypertension
options.D: Urinary retention

explanation: If a patient already cannot empty their bladder, giving a drug that relaxes the bladder even more will make retention much worse.

question: Why do circulating hormones only affect certain specific tissues rather than every cell in the body?

options.A: Only target cells possess the specific receptors for that hormone
options.B: Blood flow is completely blocked from non-target organs
options.C: Hormones are instantly destroyed if they touch wrong cells
options.D: Non-target cells actively repel circulating chemical messengers

explanation: A hormone travels everywhere via the blood, but only cells with matching receptors can receive the message and respond. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h1)

question: Why do droplet precautions only require a standard mask within a short distance of the patient?

options.A: Large respiratory droplets are heavy and quickly fall to the ground
options.B: Healthy lungs naturally repel moisture droplets from outside
options.C: Coughing only produces germs that travel upwards
options.D: Droplet nuclei dissolve instantly upon touching room air

explanation: Heavy droplets generated by coughing or sneezing usually drop within one meter, meaning they do not float long distances like airborne particles. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h4)

question: Who are some of the best local partners for community health nurses working to prevent FGM?

options.A: Religious leaders, school teachers, and women's groups
options.B: International lawyers and foreign embassy officials only
options.C: Private security guards and military personnel exclusively
options.D: Traditional cutters and commercial blade suppliers

explanation: Correct! Teaming up with respected community voices helps nurses reach families effectively and spread the message against FGM.

question: What is the main goal of giving blood pressure (antihypertensive) medications?

options.A: To cure the underlying structural heart disease permanently
options.B: To reduce cardiovascular risks and prevent target organ damage
options.C: To lower the resting heart rate below sixty beats per minute
options.D: To increase the total volume of circulating blood plasma

explanation: Great job! Blood pressure meds are meant to protect vital organs like your heart, brain, and kidneys from the wear-and-tear of high pressure over time.

question: How can community health nurses best fight social stigma against disability?

options.A: By ignoring cultural beliefs entirely without discussion
options.B: By focusing solely on medication management in clinics
options.C: Through patient advocacy and public health education
options.D: By keeping affected individuals hidden safely at home

explanation: Brilliant! Education and speaking up help clear away harmful myths, replacing fear with inclusion and understanding.

question: Why should a nurse manager mix and match different motivational theories on the ward?

options.A: Different nurses have unique professional needs and career drivers
options.B: Only one theory applies to nurses working night shifts
options.C: Using a single theory is illegal under labor laws
options.D: Hospital accreditation boards require all theories to be used equally

explanation: Spot on! Every nurse is different. What motivates a fresh graduate might be totally different from what drives a senior nursing officer.

question: A patient sits up on the side of the bed in preparation for walking and immediately reports feeling very dizzy and lightheaded. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Lay the patient back down and postpone ambulation
options.B: Administer a strong pain medication immediately
options.C: Force them to stand up quickly to test their balance
options.D: Leave the room to fetch a wheelchair right away

explanation: Dizziness means the blood pressure has dropped too low upon sitting up, so returning them to a flat position keeps them safe from fainting. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h2)

question: What is a common patient misconception regarding injections that nurses should actively address?

options.A: Expecting nurses to reuse needles to save money for the clinic
options.B: Assuming all vaccines contain active live viruses that cause severe disease
options.C: Thinking that single-use syringes can be washed at home with hot water
options.D: Believing injections are always superior or faster than oral drugs for any illness

explanation: Many patients demand injections unnecessarily, unaware that safe oral medications are often just as effective and carry fewer risks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h7)

question: Which injection route is standard for administering the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine to a newborn?

options.A: Deep intravenous bolus injection into a peripheral vein
options.B: Intramuscular injection into the thigh muscle
options.C: Intradermal injection to create a shallow skin wheal
options.D: Subcutaneous injection into the fatty arm tissue

explanation: BCG is given intradermally into the superficial layers of the skin, typically on the upper arm, producing a characteristic small raised bleb. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h6)

question: When blood pressure drops too low, how does aldosterone help bring it back up?

options.A: By forcing the heart to beat slower and weaker
options.B: By causing blood vessels to instantly dilate wide
options.C: By stopping the release of antidiuretic hormone
options.D: By causing the kidneys to reabsorb sodium and water

explanation: Aldosterone holds onto salt (sodium) in the kidneys. Water naturally follows salt into the blood, increasing your fluid volume and raising your blood pressure!

question: Why do supply chain delays and food spoilage lead to higher prices at the grocery store?

options.A: Transport companies reduce their fees when food rots in transit
options.B: Retailers must raise prices on surviving goods to cover the financial losses of spoiled food
options.C: Spoiled food makes the remaining items taste better and command higher prices
options.D: Governments penalize stores by lowering the tax on fresh produce

explanation: Sellers offset the money lost from spoiled inventory by charging more for the food that successfully reaches shelves. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h5)

question: A family member shows signs of severe, prolonged distress months after a patient's death, unable to perform basic daily tasks. What condition does this suggest?

options.A: Temporary fatigue from caregiving
options.B: Standard anticipatory mourning
options.C: Complicated or prolonged grief disorder
options.D: Normal adjustment to everyday life

explanation: When grief remains intense and impairs daily functioning long after the loss, it may require specialized counseling support. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h6)

question: What happens during the acrosome reaction when a sperm reaches the outer layers of an egg?

options.A: Enzymes are released from the sperm head to digest a path through protective layers
options.B: The sperm tail falls off completely to anchor the head inside the follicle
options.C: The egg swallows the entire sperm tail without using any chemical help
options.D: Protective antibodies coat the sperm to prevent premature entry

explanation: Think of the acrosome as a tiny chemical drill at the tip of the sperm head, releasing special enzymes to clear a pathway through the egg's defenses.

question: What is the primary purpose of increased maternal aldosterone production during gestation?

options.A: To maintain a high level of urinary calcium excretion
options.B: To directly stimulate smooth muscle contractions in the uterus
options.C: To prevent dangerous spikes in maternal blood pressure
options.D: To help manage the large expansion of maternal blood volume

explanation: Elevated aldosterone encourages the kidneys to retain sodium and water, which supports the necessary increase in total blood volume needed to supply the placenta. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h2)

question: Why are community health nurses in a great position to promote cancer prevention?

options.A: They are the only healthcare professionals permitted to diagnose tumors
options.B: They hold exclusive authority over national public health budgets
options.C: They interact directly with individuals and families on a regular basis
options.D: They spend all their time working inside high-tech molecular laboratories

explanation: Because nurses interact regularly with everyday people and families, they are perfectly placed to teach about risk factors and encourage healthy habits. Well done! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is a huge advantage of molecular tests over traditional lab cultures?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need to collect any patient specimen
options.B: They allow the nurse to administer antibiotics without a doctor's order
options.C: They can identify germs much faster without waiting days for colonies to grow
options.D: They are always much cheaper than any other laboratory test

explanation: Great job! Molecular tests look straight at the DNA, saving us from waiting days for bacteria to grow in a dish.

question: Why do cardiovascular complications develop in patients with long-term heart conditions?

options.A: Patients always stop taking their drugs entirely
options.B: Blood vessels suddenly become immune to pressure
options.C: Eating salt immediately cures heart disease
options.D: The heart's backup coping methods eventually fail under ongoing stress

explanation: Just like working out too hard without rest, the extra work the heart does to manage a disease eventually wears down its muscles and structure, leading to new problems.

question: Which of these is a great example of a positive feedback loop?

options.A: Insulin lowering high blood sugar back to normal
options.B: Parathyroid hormone raising low blood calcium levels
options.C: Oxytocin increasing uterine contractions during labor
options.D: Thyroid hormone stopping pituitary TSH production

explanation: Positive feedback pushes a process further and faster until the goal is met, just like oxytocin intensifying contractions until baby arrives!

question: Why is promoting local Nigerian foods better than relying on foreign supplements for community health?

options.A: Local foods have zero carbohydrates and eliminate all diseases
options.B: Local foods are affordable, culturally acceptable, and readily available
options.C: Local foods never spoil even without refrigeration
options.D: Imported supplements are always illegal to prescribe in clinics

explanation: Using familiar, accessible foodstuffs empowers families to eat well long-term without breaking the bank.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical result of eating a lot of junk food or processed snacks during adolescence?

options.A: Poor long-term bone health
options.B: Stronger skeletal bone density
options.C: Increased risk of iron deficiency
options.D: Erratic eating schedules

explanation: Processed foods lack key nutrients like calcium, so they certainly won't build stronger bones!

question: A young woman who had FGM as a child comes to your clinic with painful periods and trouble passing urine. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: A newly developed hormonal imbalance
options.B: An acute bacterial kidney infection
options.C: Scar tissue buildup and urethral obstruction
options.D: Normal physiological changes of aging

explanation: Years of healing leave tough scar tissue that can block the urinary and vaginal openings, making both urination and menstruation very painful.

question: What is a major advantage of using questionnaires in nursing research?

options.A: They guarantee a 100 percent response rate from participants
options.B: They can efficiently gather data from large numbers of people
options.C: They completely eliminate the possibility of human bias
options.D: They allow researchers to perform deep physical exams

explanation: Questionnaires can be distributed widely via mail or the internet, making it easy to collect data from large populations quickly. Excellent job!

question: How does maintaining strict confidentiality during post-abortion counseling help the patient?

options.A: It builds trust and encourages women to seek timely care without fear of judgment
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never experience another unplanned pregnancy
options.C: It prevents the hospital administration from billing the patient for services
options.D: It replaces the need for physical medical interventions during an emergency

explanation: Exactly! Because of heavy social stigma, clients fear being judged. Absolute privacy helps them feel safe and cared for.

question: In reproductive health, what does the abbreviation mCPR stand for?

options.A: Midwife Contraceptive Practice Rule
options.B: Modern Contraceptive Prevalence Rate
options.C: Monthly Clinical Patient Record
options.D: Maternal Child Protection Ratio

explanation: Think of mCPR as a handy way to track how many women of childbearing age are currently using modern family planning methods. You've got this!

question: What does the first menstrual period (menarche) mainly tell us about a young girl?

options.A: Full adult nutritional stores
options.B: Maximum skeletal height achievement
options.C: The beginning of reproductive capability
options.D: Complete closure of the pelvic growth plates

explanation: Well done! Menarche shows her body can now release eggs, but remember: it doesn't mean her pelvic bones are fully grown for safe childbirth yet.

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a secondary (acquired) immunodeficiency?

options.A: Suppression caused by chemotherapy drugs
options.B: A genetic enzyme defect present since birth
options.C: Immune damage resulting from an HIV infection
options.D: Malnutrition leading to weakened white blood cell function

explanation: A condition present right from birth is a primary (congenital) issue. Conditions like HIV, malnutrition, and chemo damage a previously healthy immune system later in life, making them acquired.

question: Why do large, complex proteins usually make much better antigens than small, simple molecules?

options.A: They offer more complex structures for immune cells to recognize and process
options.B: They are heavy enough to physically crush invading white blood cells
options.C: They prevent the body from ever producing any antibodies at all
options.D: They dissolve completely in blood plasma without needing any digestion

explanation: Big, detailed structures give immune cells plenty of unique shapes to grab onto, making it much easier to mount a strong defense.

question: At what age group are public health programs primarily targeting the HPV vaccine for the best results?

options.A: Pre-adolescent girls aged 9 to 14 years
options.B: Infants during their routine immunization schedule
options.C: Adult women over the age of 50 years
options.D: Pregnant women during prenatal clinic visits

explanation: Correct! The HPV vaccine works best when given before any exposure to the virus through sexual activity, which is why pre-teens aged 9 to 14 are the main target group.

question: Why is immediacy important when applying the Hot Stove Rule?

options.A: It allows the manager to go home earlier
options.B: It connects the consequence directly to the rule violation
options.C: It prevents other staff members from noticing the error
options.D: It gives the nurse less time to defend themselves

explanation: Acting quickly ensures the employee clearly links the disciplinary action to their specific misbehavior. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h3)

question: What is formed at the very end of the clotting process to firmly seal a damaged blood vessel?

options.A: Soluble fibrinogen
options.B: Unbound platelets
options.C: Inactive thrombin
options.D: Stable fibrin mesh

explanation: At the finish line of the clotting cascade, fibrinogen turns into a strong, stable fibrin mesh that holds the blood clot firmly in place like a net.

question: What is the difference between monitoring and evaluation in community health programs?

options.A: Monitoring deals only with finance, while evaluation deals only with drugs
options.B: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.C: Monitoring is ongoing during the project, while evaluation assesses final outcomes
options.D: Monitoring happens after the project closes, while evaluation happens before

explanation: Monitoring happens continuously as activities are implemented, whereas evaluation measures the ultimate success or impact of the project at the end. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h7)

question: A female patient comes to the clinic with ongoing pelvic pain, constant headaches, and severe anxiety that doctors can't quite explain. What should you keep in mind?

options.A: An adverse reaction to routine vaccination
options.B: An acute bacterial infection of the kidneys
options.C: A congenital structural defect in the pelvis
options.D: A history of physical or psychological abuse

explanation: Great thinking! Unexplained chronic aches and high anxiety can often be the body's way of showing the hidden scars of past abuse.

question: Which transmission route involves pathogens spreading via contaminated inanimate objects like door handles or instruments?

options.A: Airborne droplet transmission
options.B: Vector-borne transmission
options.C: Direct contact transmission
options.D: Indirect contact transmission

explanation: Indirect contact occurs when a susceptible host touches a surface or object that harbors infectious agents. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h3)

question: How do deficiencies in calcium and vitamin D primarily contribute to fracture risk?

options.A: They increase sudden blood pressure spikes
options.B: They cause muscles to pull too hard on joints
options.C: They stop the bone from forming a blood clot
options.D: They impair proper bone mineralization and strength

explanation: Calcium and vitamin D are essential building blocks for strong bone matrix; without them, bones lose their structural density. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h4)

question: What hemoglobin value means a laboring woman has severe anaemia?

options.A: Between 10.0 and 10.9 g/dL
options.B: Below 9.0 g/dL
options.C: Below 12.0 g/dL
options.D: Below 7.0 g/dL

explanation: A reading under 7.0 g/dL is a red flag for severe anaemia that needs immediate medical action.

question: How far do infectious respiratory droplets typically travel through the air?

options.A: Throughout the ventilation system
options.B: Up to ten meters
options.C: Across an entire building
options.D: Less than one meter

explanation: That's right! Respiratory droplets are quite heavy, so gravity pulls them down fast. They rarely travel farther than a meter from the person coughing or talking.

question: Which common hormonal condition is a frequent cause of chronic anovulation and irregular periods?

options.A: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Uterine leiomyoma or fibroids
options.D: Acute pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) throws off the usual hormonal balance, making it tricky for the ovaries to regularly select and release a dominant follicle.

question: What is the main artery that brings oxygen-rich blood to the tongue?

options.A: Facial artery
options.B: Maxillary artery
options.C: Lingual artery
options.D: Ascending pharyngeal artery

explanation: Easy to remember—'lingual' means tongue, so the lingual artery is the main blood supplier for tongue tissues!

question: Which level of health care serves as the first point of contact for a rural community?

options.A: Secondary Health Care
options.B: Private specialist clinics
options.C: Primary Health Care
options.D: Tertiary Health Care

explanation: Primary health centers are built right inside communities to handle everyday health needs first. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h2)

question: A patient with severe arthritis cannot walk to the bathroom or manage clothing buttons fast enough, resulting in accidental urine loss. What type of incontinence is this?

options.A: Overflow incontinence
options.B: Urge incontinence
options.C: Functional incontinence
options.D: Stress incontinence

explanation: Functional incontinence occurs when the urinary tract is fine, but physical or environmental barriers stop the person from reaching the toilet. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h3)

question: What does the presence of bacteria on a synovial fluid Gram stain indicate?

options.A: Septic arthritis
options.B: Normal joint aging
options.C: Simple osteoarthritis
options.D: Mild muscle fatigue

explanation: Bacteria in the joint space signify a severe joint infection requiring urgent antibiotic treatment. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h6)

question: What is a core responsibility of a community health nurse working with nurseries?

options.A: Managing the financial profits and tax returns of the facility
options.B: Replacing the parents as the primary legal guardian
options.C: Purchasing all commercial toys and playground equipment
options.D: Conducting health appraisals and checking immunization records

explanation: Community health nurses focus on health promotion, disease prevention, and monitoring vaccination compliance in childcare settings. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h6)

question: On a standard muscle strength scale, what does a score of zero (0) indicate?

options.A: A slight flicker of movement only
options.B: No movement or muscle contraction at all
options.C: Movement is possible against gravity
options.D: Normal strength against full resistance

explanation: A score of zero means there is total paralysis or no visible muscle movement when the patient tries to move.

question: A patient gets a bad bloodstream infection 3 days after having an IV line put in with poor hygiene. What do we call this?

options.A: A healthcare-associated infection
options.B: An unavoidable diagnostic error
options.C: A near miss incident
options.D: A never event

explanation: Exactly! When an infection is picked up while receiving care (often due to poor aseptic technique), it's a healthcare-associated infection. Good hand hygiene prevents this!

question: Why do many couples in local communities prefer traditional family planning methods?

options.A: They prevent all sexually transmitted infections
options.B: They require no active participation from partners
options.C: They offer 100 percent protection against pregnancy
options.D: They are accessible and cost-free

explanation: Because these methods don't require buying commercial products or visiting a clinic every month, they are very easy to access in communities with limited resources.

question: What routine self-care practice is strongly emphasized to patients at risk for infective endocarditis to prevent bacteria from entering the bloodstream?

options.A: Refusing all routine vaccinations at local health clinics
options.B: Drinking large quantities of palm wine daily
options.C: Maintaining good oral hygiene and regular dental check-ups
options.D: Avoiding all physical exercise for the rest of their lives

explanation: Oral bacteria can easily enter the bloodstream during dental procedures or daily hygiene, making dental care a primary prevention target for endocarditis. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h8)

question: Which sanitation practice helps stop rats and mice from taking over residential areas?

options.A: Storing harvested grains directly on bare dirt floors inside homes
options.B: Properly covering refuse bins and clearing overgrown bushes
options.C: Leaving domestic food waste uncovered in open backyard spaces
options.D: Digging shallow soakaway pits close to kitchen entrances

explanation: Spot on! Covering trash cuts off their food supply, and clearing bushes takes away their hiding spots.

question: Who is most important to involve when trying to change harmful food taboos in a rural community?

options.A: Community elders and family heads
options.B: Children under the age of five years
options.C: Foreign tourists visiting the local market
options.D: International food manufacturing companies

explanation: In our communities, elders and family heads hold the keys to tradition. If you want sustainable change, you must bring them along on the health education journey!

question: Which of these is a great example of the 'Right Assessment' in action?

options.A: Checking blood pressure before giving an antihypertensive drug
options.B: Asking the patient what their favorite food is for breakfast
options.C: Cleaning the bedside table before placing a water cup
options.D: Reading the hospital policy manual on intravenous access

explanation: Right assessment means checking vital signs or lab results first to make sure the drug is actually safe to give right now.

question: What does 'food security' mean for a population?

options.A: Storing a ten-year supply of grains in underground bunkers
options.B: Having military protection around every food warehouse
options.C: Constant physical, social, and economic access to safe and enough food
options.D: Producing every single food item inside the country's borders

explanation: Food security simply means everyone has reliable access to enough safe, nutritious food to live a healthy life.

question: What is the main reason we wash our hands before preparing food?

options.A: To activate natural sweat gland secretions
options.B: To prevent transferring harmful microbes to food
options.C: To remove natural skin oils and improve grip
options.D: To cool down the hands before touching ingredients

explanation: Simple hand hygiene stops unseen germs on our skin from hitching a ride into the food and making people sick.

question: Which neurotransmitter is primarily linked to feelings of reward, motivation, and the hallucinations seen in schizophrenia?

options.A: Dopamine
options.B: Melatonin
options.C: Serotonin
options.D: GABA

explanation: Dopamine pathways regulate reward and motivation, and overactive dopamine signaling is a major factor in psychotic symptoms like hallucinations. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why are strong people skills even more important in community nursing than in a big hospital?

options.A: Hospital nurses do not need to communicate with patients and families.
options.B: Patients in communities are more likely to reject care if they feel judged or misunderstood.
options.C: Community nurses rarely perform physical assessments or give medications.
options.D: Community settings have unlimited funding for medical technology.

explanation: Spot on! Since you are visiting people in their own private space, building a warm connection means everything. If they feel judged, they simply won't let you help.

question: Within how many hours of a possible HIV exposure should Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) be started for the best results?

options.A: Within 72 hours
options.B: Within 1 week
options.C: Within 24 days
options.D: Within 48 weeks

explanation: Time matters! Starting PEP within 72 hours gives the best chance of preventing HIV after an exposure.

question: Which Nigerian law sets the main minimum standards for factory safety and worker welfare?

options.A: The National Health Insurance Act
options.B: The Land Use Act
options.C: The Criminal Code Act
options.D: The Factories Act

explanation: You'll see this often in Nigerian public health! The Factories Act is the key law that protects workers and regulates safety conditions in Nigerian workplaces.

question: Which hormone directly stimulates the respiratory center to increase ventilation during pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Estrogen

explanation: Progesterone acts directly on the brain's respiratory center, increasing the sensitivity to carbon dioxide and prompting deeper, more frequent breathing. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h2)

question: Why is communication considered a vital part of the IEC approach rather than just giving information?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will take their prescribed medications on time.
options.B: It establishes a two-way dialogue to build trust and address community concerns.
options.C: It allows the nurse to avoid writing formal health reports.
options.D: It eliminates the need for any formal health education classes.

explanation: Communication is a two-way process that fosters trust and helps health workers understand local beliefs and fears. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h1)

question: A patient expresses deep shame and refuses visitors due to faecal incontinence. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Provide empathetic listening and discuss discreet coping strategies
options.B: Encourage the patient to ignore the problem completely
options.C: Restrict all family members from visiting permanently
options.D: Tell the patient that everyone experiences this eventually

explanation: Validating the patient's feelings and offering practical solutions helps restore dignity and reduces anxiety related to the condition. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h8)

question: What is the key difference between summarizing and synthesizing literature?

options.A: Grouping multiple studies together by themes and trends
options.B: Deleting any study that disagrees with your personal opinion
options.C: Copying abstracts word-for-word into your own paper
options.D: Listing every single article in strict chronological order

explanation: Synthesis means weaving different studies together around common themes, rather than just listing one summary after another.

question: What is the core message of the contingency approach to management?

options.A: Every hospital must use the exact same leadership rules
options.B: Financial incentives are the only way to motivate staff
options.C: Managers should never change their personal leadership style
options.D: The best management style depends on the specific situation

explanation: Contingency theory teaches that leaders must adapt their approach based on the unique demands of each scenario. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which drug name is given by the manufacturer and always starts with a capital letter?

options.A: Official name
options.B: Brand name
options.C: Chemical name
options.D: Generic name

explanation: Brand names (like Panadol) are created by companies for marketing and are always capitalized, unlike generic names.

question: Which part of the nervous system kicks in during a 'fight-or-flight' stress response?

options.A: Parasympathetic division
options.B: Central division
options.C: Sympathetic division
options.D: Somatic division

explanation: Spot on! The sympathetic system pumps up your heart rate and gets your body ready for action when you're stressed or scared.

question: What usually takes up the biggest slice of a nursing unit's operating budget?

options.A: Office stationery and printing
options.B: Patient dietary and meal trays
options.C: Staff salaries and labor costs
options.D: Building maintenance and paint

explanation: Nursing is all about people! Because healthcare relies so heavily on hands-on care, staff salaries and labor make up the highest cost in almost any unit.

question: A patient is given a drug that blocks acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction. What happens as a result?

options.A: Muscle relaxation and paralysis
options.B: Increased action potential speed
options.C: Rapid muscle hypertrophy
options.D: Uncontrolled muscle spasms

explanation: If the chemical messenger can't deliver its message because the receptors are blocked, the muscle simply cannot receive the signal to contract. That leads to relaxation and paralysis! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a stock card in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To record the daily vital signs and health status of admitted patients
options.B: To document the financial salaries and allowances of hospital workers
options.C: To schedule the duty shifts and off-days of the ward nursing staff
options.D: To track the exact quantity and movement of a specific supply item

explanation: A stock card functions as a ledger specifically designed to monitor inventory levels, showing when items enter and leave the ward. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h1)

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a hospital?

options.A: To provide free medications to all visiting patients
options.B: To maintain a continuous supply of essential drugs through sales revenue
options.C: To fund the construction of new hospital wards and laboratories
options.D: To generate profit for the hospital management board

explanation: Think of the DRF like a self-sustaining cycle! Money from drug sales is used right back to buy fresh stock, so the pharmacy never runs dry.

question: What is a common trigger for autonomic dysreflexia in a patient with a spinal cord injury?

options.A: Eating a high-protein meal
options.B: Bladder distension or a full bladder
options.C: Rising from a lying position
options.D: Speaking too loudly

explanation: A distended bladder or bowel impaction sends pain signals up the spinal cord that get blocked, causing a dangerous reflex surge in blood pressure. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h4)

question: Why might a patient's surgical incision fail to heal properly due to poor diet?

options.A: The body lacks the necessary chemical building blocks for tissue repair
options.B: Patients who eat poorly refuse to take their prescribed painkillers
options.C: Dietary deficiencies completely stop blood circulation
options.D: Poor nutrition automatically causes surgical site infections

explanation: Cellular growth and tissue mending require specific nutrients like proteins and vitamins; without them, the body cannot effectively close wounds. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h1)

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a clinic or hospital?

options.A: To generate huge profits for hospital management
options.B: To store expired medications safely before disposal
options.C: To maintain a continuous and steady supply of essential drugs
options.D: To provide free medical treatment to all citizens

explanation: You've got this! The whole point of a DRF is to make sure essential medicines never run out. Money collected from sales is used right away to buy fresh stock. Simple and effective!

question: What is a core goal of immunization within Primary Health Care?

options.A: To treat acute bacterial infections in children
options.B: To replace the need for clean water and nutrition
options.C: To interrupt transmission of vaccine-preventable diseases
options.D: To completely eliminate all known human illnesses

explanation: The main purpose of immunization in public health is to prevent specific infectious diseases and stop them from spreading in communities. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h1)

question: Why do night-shift nurses often find it hard to sleep during the day? Daytime light affects which hormone?

options.A: Aldosterone
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Melatonin
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Daylight tells your biological clock to keep melatonin levels low, which is why sleeping during the day after a night shift can be so tough.

question: Why is asking a patient about their recent travel and contacts so important when they have a fever?

options.A: It replaces the need for laboratory blood tests and imaging.
options.B: It helps identify exposure to specific local germs in certain areas.
options.C: It determines the exact genetic makeup of the patient.
options.D: It cures the underlying infection before medication is given.

explanation: Knowing where a patient has been is like getting a cheat code for diagnosis! It tells you what specific local germs they might have picked up.

question: What type of question should you ask if you want a patient to open up and share their feelings?

options.A: Rhetorical question
options.B: Closed-ended question
options.C: Open-ended question
options.D: Leading question

explanation: Open-ended questions give patients the freedom to talk in their own words, rather than just answering a quick 'yes' or 'no'.

question: Why might a patient feel surprisingly little pain right after a very severe full-thickness burn?

options.A: The outer skin layer blocks the pain signals from traveling
options.B: Deep muscle tissue absorbs all the initial heat energy
options.C: The body releases a large amount of natural painkillers
options.D: The nerve endings in the skin have been destroyed

explanation: Spot on! Because full-thickness burns destroy the skin completely, the nerve endings that usually send pain signals to the brain are burnt away.

question: When must a nurse choose soap and water over an alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.B: Before entering a patient room for vital signs
options.C: After touching an intact patient gown
options.D: Immediately before administering oral medication

explanation: Alcohol rubs do not clean away physical dirt or certain spore-forming bacteria effectively, requiring mechanical washing with soap and water. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h2)

question: Besides keeping your nursing license active, why is continuing education so important for daily practice?

options.A: It directly contributes to safer and better patient care outcomes
options.B: It removes the need to ever read medical textbooks again
options.C: It allows nurses to skip annual performance evaluations at work
options.D: It permanently exempts senior nurses from working night shifts

explanation: At the end of the day, everything we learn is about protecting our patients. Staying updated means fewer mistakes and safer hands at the bedside!

question: Which emotional reaction is a patient facing a terminal diagnosis most likely to experience first?

options.A: Complete emotional numbness
options.B: Relief from daily stress
options.C: Peaceful acceptance
options.D: Denial and shock

explanation: Denial is a common initial defense mechanism that helps protect the psyche from being overwhelmed by catastrophic news. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h3)

question: When does an Rh-negative person usually develop anti-Rh antibodies?

options.A: After direct exposure to Rh-positive blood
options.B: Only after multiple pregnancies regardless of blood type
options.C: Naturally during the first few weeks of life
options.D: Before birth while inside the womb

explanation: Remember, unlike ABO antibodies which are present naturally, Rh antibodies only form after the immune system has its first contact with Rh-positive cells. Great job learning this! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h3)

question: Under Nigerian law, what is the main legal ground that allows for a safe and lawful termination of pregnancy?

options.A: When the pregnancy results from consensual sex
options.B: Upon the request of both parents
options.C: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.D: In cases of severe economic hardship

explanation: You've got this! Nigerian law is very strict, allowing pregnancy termination only when it is necessary to preserve the mother's life.

question: Early in your research journey, how does having a theoretical framework help you?

options.A: Clear research questions
options.B: The hospital budget
options.C: The nursing shift schedule
options.D: Patient discharge summaries

explanation: Well done! A good framework shines a light on what you need to study, making it much easier to write sharp and focused research questions.

question: Which organisms are the most common culprits behind infections leading to oophoritis?

options.A: Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus
options.B: Candida albicans and Trichomonas vaginalis
options.C: Streptococcus pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.D: Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae

explanation: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) like chlamydia and gonorrhea are the most common primary causes of these ascending infections. Good to keep in mind for clinical practice!

question: Why are Insecticide-Treated Nets (ITNs) most effective when used while sleeping?

options.A: Anopheles mosquitoes bite mostly at night when people are asleep
options.B: It prevents mosquitoes from laying eggs inside household water pots
options.C: The chemical on the net repels daytime flies and cockroaches
options.D: It completely stops the flow of humid air into the bedroom

explanation: You got it! Since malaria mosquitoes love to hunt during the night, sleeping under a treated net hits them right when they are most active.

question: Why is time critical when starting Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) for HIV after an exposure?

options.A: Hospital insurance only covers the drugs on the first day
options.B: Delayed treatment makes the medication toxic to the kidneys
options.C: PEP works best when started very soon after exposure, ideally within 72 hours
options.D: The virus disappears from the bloodstream after three days

explanation: Starting medications quickly stops the virus from replicating and establishing a permanent infection in the body. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h7)

question: What is a classic sign of cervical irritation that often shows up after sexual intercourse?

options.A: Severe lower back stiffness
options.B: Post-coital bleeding
options.C: Intermittent abdominal swelling
options.D: Sudden loss of bladder control

explanation: Spot on! When the cervix is inflamed and fragile, any physical touch or rubbing during sex can easily trigger light bleeding.

question: What happens inside the body to cause lymphoma?

options.A: Lymph vessels become blocked and burst
options.B: Abnormal lymphocytes multiply out of control and form tumors
options.C: The spleen stops filtering old cells
options.D: Bone marrow permanently stops making white cells

explanation: Lymphoma happens when those protective white blood cells (lymphocytes) go wild, dividing without stopping and building up in the lymph nodes.

question: Why is keeping things confidential so vital when teaching youth about sexual health?

options.A: It prevents parents from ever speaking with healthcare providers
options.B: It is required by law only for adult patients over the age of twenty-one
options.C: It builds trust and encourages adolescents to seek necessary health guidance
options.D: It guarantees that the adolescent will never experience an illness

explanation: You got it! Teens are much more likely to ask for help and get correct information when they know their private worries are safe with you.

question: A patient with severe nerve pain after shingles is given an anticonvulsant. Why?

options.A: To lower systemic blood pressure and reduce cardiac workload
options.B: To destroy the viral infection causing the localized skin rash
options.C: To calm hyperactive nerve impulses transmitting abnormal pain signals
options.D: To completely replace the need for any physical therapy sessions

explanation: Damaged nerves love to fire random, painful zaps. Anticonvulsants quiet those wild nerve signals right down.

question: A patient is suffering from severe diarrhea and vomiting. What condition are they most at risk for?

options.A: Fluid volume deficit
options.B: Metabolic alkalosis
options.C: Respiratory alkalosis
options.D: Fluid volume excess

explanation: When fluids leave the body too fast from both ends, fluid volume drops quickly. That's why rehydration is usually the very first order of business!

question: Why do inhaled drug particles need to be between 1 and 5 microns in size?

options.A: To prevent the medication from dissolving too quickly in saliva
options.B: To ensure the particles are completely filtered out by the nose
options.C: To make the powder heavy enough to drop straight down the throat
options.D: To successfully reach the smaller bronchioles and alveoli

explanation: Think of particle size like a key fitting a lock! Tiny particles (1 to 5 microns) are just small enough to bypass the nose and throat filters and travel deep down into the lungs where the real work happens.

question: Why does the timing of certain reproductive health tests matter so much?

options.A: Infection rates are highest right after ovulation occurs
options.B: Hospitals only have laboratory reagents available on specific days of the month
options.C: Patients are too weak to undergo procedures during the first week of bleeding
options.D: Hormone levels and uterine lining thickness change during the menstrual cycle

explanation: Exactly! Hormones and tissue structures shift naturally all month long, so tests need to be timed right to get accurate results.

question: What is your main duty as a nurse when a patient comes in with complications from an illegal abortion?

options.A: Report her to security before starting any fluids
options.B: Lecture her on the morality of her actions
options.C: Provide immediate, non-judgmental life-saving emergency care
options.D: Refuse treatment until the police arrive

explanation: As a professional nurse, saving a life always comes first. We treat every patient with care, empathy, and zero judgment.

question: A nurse notices patient call bells take much longer to answer during evening shifts. What is the best systems-thinking response?

options.A: Map out evening workloads, staffing numbers, and task layouts to find the bottleneck
options.B: Tell the evening nurses they are lazy and need to walk faster
options.C: Ignore it because evening shifts are always chaotic
options.D: Punish the nurse sitting closest to the front desk

explanation: Looking for structural bottlenecks instead of throwing blame is the core of systems thinking in nursing leadership.

question: Why is regular monitoring and evaluation essential for public health campaigns against harmful practices?

options.A: To collect financial fines from communities that fail to comply
options.B: To replace local nurses with international researchers
options.C: To create strict academic exams for regional healthcare workers
options.D: To measure progress, track prevalence, and adjust ineffective strategies

explanation: Tracking data shows whether programs are actually reducing harmful practices or if new approaches are needed. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h8)

question: A young adult patient has lost a large amount of blood from a trauma, yet their blood pressure remains normal. What is the best explanation for this?

options.A: Young adults are immune to the effects of hypovolemic shock
options.B: The bleeding has completely stopped on its own
options.C: Strong blood vessel constriction is temporarily hiding the blood loss
options.D: The blood loss is minor and requires no further observation

question: Why are growth hormone and thyroid hormones so critical during infancy and childhood?

options.B: They maintain normal calcium balance in the bones
options.C: They control the immediate fight-or-flight stress reaction
options.D: They coordinate normal skeletal growth and brain maturation

question: What is dumping syndrome?

options.A: An allergic reaction to intravenous protein solutions

options.C: The inability of the kidneys to filter waste products after major surgery
options.D: The total stoppage of bowel movements for over a week

question: How does vascular dementia primarily develop, setting it apart from Alzheimer's disease?

options.A: It only affects physical movement without touching memory
options.B: It is triggered strictly by nutritional deficiencies in old age
options.C: It is caused by reduced blood flow to the brain from problems like strokes
options.D: It develops entirely from sudden viral infections of the nervous tissue

explanation: Spot on! Vascular dementia happens when blood supply to the brain is blocked or reduced—often due to tiny strokes—starving brain cells of oxygen.

question: What is the primary goal of harm reduction strategies in community nursing?

options.A: To minimize negative health and social consequences of drug use
options.B: To force every patient into immediate inpatient rehab
options.C: To arrest individuals who possess illegal substances
options.D: To ignore drug use until the person asks for help

explanation: Great thinking! Harm reduction is all about keeping people safe, preventing infections, and saving lives—meeting patients right where they are with compassion.

question: What is a key nursing action to prevent bedsores (pressure injuries) in immobile residents?

options.A: Applying strong antiseptic ointment to all bony areas
options.B: Limiting fluid intake to prevent skin moisture
options.C: Keeping the resident in bed twenty-four hours a day
options.D: Implementing regular repositioning schedules

explanation: Spot on! Turning and repositioning patients regularly takes the weight off bony spots, keeping their skin safe and healthy.

question: What is the main reason a patient must stay NPO (nothing by mouth) before surgery?

options.A: To reduce the cost of hospital meals
options.B: To speed up post-operative wound healing
options.C: To prevent sudden spikes in blood pressure
options.D: To prevent aspiration during anesthesia

explanation: Keeping the stomach empty stops food or vomit from rising up and entering the lungs while the patient is asleep under anesthesia. Safety first!

question: Which patients should receive Standard Precautions?

options.A: Every patient in the healthcare setting
options.B: Only patients with weak immune systems
options.C: Only patients admitted to the emergency room
options.D: Only patients with confirmed infections

explanation: Always treat every patient with Standard Precautions! We treat everyone as if they could carry an infection, keeping both them and us safe.

question: Which high-touch surface in a patient room requires frequent routine disinfection?

options.A: Bedside tables and bed rails
options.B: The inside of closed closet drawers
options.C: Carpeted flooring under the bed
options.D: The ceiling tiles above the bed

question: What is the most common form of dementia seen among older adults?

options.A: Vascular dementia
options.B: Frontotemporal dementia
options.C: Lewy body dementia
options.D: Alzheimer's disease

explanation: You'll see this a lot in clinical practice! Alzheimer's disease accounts for the vast majority of all dementia cases worldwide.

question: What is the main purpose of tilting the X-ray table into different angles during a barium swallow?

options.A: To drain excess stomach fluids before the contrast is given

options.C: To prevent the patient from falling asleep during the procedure

question: What advice should you give a patient receiving treatment for a bacterial STI regarding sex?

options.A: Resume intercourse immediately once the burning sensation starts to fade
options.B: Limit intercourse to protected methods without needing partner treatment
options.C: Abstain from sexual activity until he and his partner have finished treatment
options.D: Use oil-based lubricants to prevent transmission while taking oral tablets

explanation: No sex until both partners finish their treatment course! This stops the dreaded 'ping-pong' effect of passing the infection right back to each other.

question: What does food fortification mean?

options.A: Adding essential vitamins and minerals to commonly eaten foods during processing
options.B: Storing harvested grains in airtight silos to prevent insect damage
options.C: Cooking traditional meals with extra salt and local spices
options.D: Growing crops using chemical fertilizers to increase crop yield

explanation: You got it! Fortification is like a health boost added right into everyday foods (like flour or salt) to protect whole communities from deficiencies. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which group of vitamins is more likely to build up in the body and cause toxicity if taken in excess for a long time?

options.A: Ascorbic acid compounds
options.B: Water-soluble vitamins
options.C: Fat-soluble vitamins
options.D: B-complex vitamins

explanation: Exactly! Fat-soluble vitamins get stored in the liver and fatty tissues instead of being peed out, so too much can cause a buildup.

question: What is the primary driving factor behind gender-based violence in most societies?

options.A: Sudden economic inflation within households
options.B: A lack of religious devotion in the community
options.C: Unequal power relations and patriarchal norms
options.D: Genetic predispositions toward aggressive behavior

explanation: GBV is deeply driven by structural inequalities and cultural beliefs that promote dominance and control over specific genders. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h1)

question: When helping a Nigerian patient plan a healthy, balanced local diet, which food combination is best?

options.A: High-fat fried snacks consumed without any protein or vegetable source
options.B: Yam or cassava served with beans, fish, and green leafy vegetable soup
options.C: Strictly white refined sugar dissolved in large quantities of clean water
options.D: Imported processed canned foods supplemented with synthetic energy drinks

explanation: Wonderful! Combining local energy staples like yam or cassava with protein (beans, fish) and nutrient-rich green leaves gives a complete, culturally wonderful meal.

question: Why is even a small, subtle change in one body system so risky for a critically ill patient?

options.A: It can quickly lead to multi-organ collapse and emergency
options.B: It only affects the specific organ without causing other issues
options.C: It means lab values are completely normal
options.D: It usually indicates that the patient is ready for discharge

explanation: Think of it like a house of cards—very sick patients have little backup energy, so a small glitch can rapidly cascade into a bigger emergency.

question: What does 'self-financing' mean for a DRF scheme?

options.A: It generates enough revenue from sales to buy replacement stock
options.B: It borrows money from private banks whenever stocks get low
options.C: It relies entirely on yearly donations from foreign countries
options.D: It receives unlimited free drugs from the central ministry

explanation: Great job! Self-financing just means the fund keeps itself alive through patient payments instead of waiting for outside help.

question: Why is studying maternal morbidity just as crucial as looking at maternal mortality?

options.A: Morbidity data is much easier to collect in rural hospitals than mortality numbers
options.B: Mortality rates have dropped to zero globally, making morbidity the only priority
options.C: It focuses solely on the health status of the newborn baby after delivery
options.D: It highlights the hidden burden of long-term suffering and disability survivors face

explanation: For every woman who sadly passes away, many more live with severe, lifelong health issues from pregnancy complications. Understanding this helps us provide better care for mothers in our communities!

question: A nurse is planning care for a newly admitted client with major depressive disorder. What is the best immediate action?

options.C: Focus exclusively on teaching the client about complex surgical procedures
options.D: Assess the client for active suicidal ideation and ensure a safe environment

explanation: Safety first! Major depressive disorder means you must always screen for self-harm and keep the environment secure. You're thinking like a true professional.

question: Why does substance use in teenagers often escalate faster than in adults?

options.A: Teenagers have fully developed brains that tolerate drugs better
options.B: Teenage brains approach risks differently, leading to faster escalation
options.C: Adolescents are biologically immune to physical dependence
options.D: Adults only use prescription drugs while teenagers use illegal ones

explanation: Spot on! The developing teenage brain processes risk and reward differently, which makes it easier to move quickly from trying something once to dependence.

question: Which health check is most crucial before giving oral medications to a patient with advanced neurological degeneration?

options.A: Checking how much water they drank today
options.B: Assessing the patient's swallowing ability
options.C: Testing their immediate memory
options.D: Measuring their handgrip strength

question: Which screening test uses a low-dose X-ray to spot tiny lumps and microcalcifications before anyone can even feel them?

options.A: Clinical inspection
options.B: Breast self-examination

options.D: Ultrasound scanning
